Hi Tim / Sarah —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about Acme AI's search/ranking workflow and the constraints you're evaluating. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Call recap (high level)
- Primary goal: improve rerank recall and reduce tail latency for product search on the storefront (customer-facing).
- Current infra: vector DB (managed) + custom ANN; embeddings produced offline at 1536 dims; reranker is TF-based re-ranker used as a second-stage.
- Pain points: p95 retrieval latency spikes during traffic bursts (~350–600ms), cost of 1536-dim embeddings at scale, and inconsistent recall@10 across some query classes.

Competition & evaluation notes you raised
- You're comparing Redwood against hyperscaler inference (Bedrock/Vertex) and a self-hosted approach. Key decision criteria: latency (p95), recall@k (k=10), per-embed unit cost, and operational simplicity.

Proposed benchmark plan (short) — attached a one-pager with the details: redwood_rerank_benchmarks_plan.pdf
- Data: you to share the 10–20k test queries + ground-truth relevance labels (CSV OK) — can use the small sample you already mentioned.
- Baselines: your current infra (self-hosted), hyperscaler API (you said Bedrock), Redwood hosted tests (same model family + quantized variant).
- Metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, retrieval latency (p50/p95), tokens/sec for reranker, and cost per 1M embeddings + cost per 1M reranker tokens.
- Configs to test: embedding dims (768 vs 1536), index type (IVF/PQ vs HNSW), and model quantization.
- Success criteria (suggested): improve recall@10 by >=3% over current baseline OR reduce embedding cost by >=30% for same recall, while keeping p95 retrieval below 250ms for typical shard sizes.

Next steps
1) Timothy — please share the test set CSV and any existing baseline numbers you have for recall@10 and p95 retrieval latency (feel free to drop in the Drive link).
2) We'll run an initial Redwood-hosted benchmark on a 10k query sample and share numbers within 3 business days.
3) If useful, we can coordinate an A/B run where we route a small percentage of live traffic to Redwood Dedicated for a 48–72h pass.

I've attached the benchmark plan, a small sample eval script (sample_eval_script.py), and a CSV template (20260402-acme-test-set.csv) — see attachments. CC'ing Aditya to help design the exact experiment parameters and run the first tests.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the clear plan. Quick answers and clarifications from our side:

- We'll share a 12k query sample with labels by EOD today (dropbox link below). It includes a mix of head/tail queries.
- Current baseline numbers (approx): recall@10 = 0.72 (avg over sample), p95 retrieval latency = 420ms (our managed DB + current ANN cluster during peak), embedding compute cost ~= $1,200 / 1M embeddings at 1536 dims (incl. preproc).
- Hyperscaler numbers: Bedrock run (single-shot) gives similar recall ~0.70 but p95 is better in some cases (~220–300ms) — informed by previous PoC. The question for us is consistency at scale and unit cost.

We have two constraints that matter for the pilot:
1) Latency target: p95 overall retrieval + rerank should be < 300ms for most customer-facing queries.
2) Cost: we'd like to see potential to cut per-embed compute + storage costs by at least 25% at parity of recall.

Dropbox: https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/abcd1234/acme-rerank-test-set

We'll also share a short access policy doc (we'll redact PII). Let us know any infra hints (index config, batch sizes) you'd like us to apply on our side.

—Tim
VP Engineering | Acme AI

Thanks Tim — got the dropbox link and the baseline numbers, very helpful. Quick technical note and the experiment we're going to kick off:

Planned Redwood benchmark (what we'll run)
- Dataset: your 12k queries + labels (we'll sample 10k for the first pass).
- Embedding configs: 1536 (your current), 768 (reduced-dim), and a quantized 1536 variant using 8-bit quantization.
- Indexes: HNSW (low-latency) + IVF+PQ (high-density) where appropriate.
- Reranker: same architecture as your TF reranker (replay logits) to get fair apples-to-apples.
- Measurement windows: steady-run (10k Qs without concurrency) + burst-run (simulate concurrent spikes to measure p95).

Early hypotheses
- 768-dim should reduce embed storage/cost by ~40% and—if the model family is tuned—may only lose ~1–2% recall@10 on average classes, but might underperform on tail queries.
- IVF+PQ will generally be cheaper but may increase p95; HNSW tuned with small efSearch should hit your p95 targets but cost more.

Aditya will run the first pass today — Aditya, can you: 1) confirm the cluster config you want for the burst-run (cpu/gpu), and 2) capture p50/p95 for both retrieval and reranker stages separately?

Tim — we'll post results to the Drive link in ~48–72 hours. If the first pass looks promising I'd propose a 48-hour live A/B to validate on production traffic.

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Tim / Marissa —

I spun up the test harness and ran the first 10k-sample steady-run this morning. Quick preliminary numbers (first pass):

Config A — Current baseline (replayed):
- recall@10: 0.72
- retrieval p50/p95: 85ms / 410ms
- end-to-end p95 (retrieval + rerank): ~520ms

Config B — Redwood hosted (1536, quantized 8-bit):
- recall@10: 0.74
- retrieval p50/p95: 70ms / 230ms
- end-to-end p95: ~310ms
- estimated embedding cost: ~ $820 / 1M (includes quantized storage savings + lower runtime GPU cost)

Config C — Redwood hosted (768 dims):
- recall@10: 0.71
- retrieval p50/p95: 60ms / 210ms
- end-to-end p95: ~285ms
- estimated embedding cost: ~ $480 / 1M

Notes / caveats:
- Tail queries: we did see a ~4% drop in recall@10 on a small subset of long-tail queries for the 768 config (we'll break those out in the full report).
- Burst-run numbers are next — I'm running a 5x concurrency spike to capture p95 amplification and will post updated p95s later today.
- Attached is the raw CSV of run results (I'll upload the full results to the Drive link).

If these numbers look reasonable to you, next recommended step is a small live A/B for 48 hours to validate the end-to-end user impact. Given your latency requirement (p95 < 300ms), both Redwood configs look promising on these steady runs.

Happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk the numbers.

—Aditya
